solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Preview of what follows 19

definitions.meaning: a short film shown ahead of a release to advertise it
19 across is PARK, and the word that comes after it gives a site for mobile homes

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a sneak look at what comes next after item nineteen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19 refers to the theme answer at 19 across; several answers in this puzzle are kinds of park.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a film preview is a short advertising clip; also a trailer park is a mobile-home site.

clue.text: Belief is held by other people

indicators.note: held by others means kept inside them

parts.note: them, as opposed to us

explanation.surface: A conviction is described as one that other people hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods, so it is a creed or faith.

clue.text: Stars with city lawyer

parts.note: and means together with
Rome, the Italian capital
DA is a US district attorney

explanation.surface: Celebrities are seen out with an urban lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like celebrities but means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Andromeda is a constellation, a named group of stars.

clue.text: Shocking cover up sport concealed

indicators.note: a piece concealed in another is tucked inside it

parts.note: a lid covers a container

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A sensational cover-up, with a sporting scandal hushed.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union; in a down entry 'up' reads it bottom to top, and 'concealed' hides the result in the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lurid describes something sensational and shocking, such as gory details.

clue.text: A children's confection covered in fruit

indicators.note: a confection is something concocted, so the letters are made up into a new form

parts.note: the fodder is A plus CHILDREN; the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A children's sweet treat smothered in fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confection' rearranges A CHILDREN (the 's adds no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Compound: laden means heavily loaded, so richly loaded with fruit, as a well-stocked tree or cake is.

clue.text: Court one of 12 19

definitions.meaning: the royal court in Britain is formally the Court of ...
one of the twelve apostles of Jesus
19 across is PARK, and ... Park is a royal park in central London

explanation.surface: A court case about one person out of twelve, perhaps a juror.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: ambassadors are accredited to the Court of St James's, James was an apostle, and St James's Park is a London park beside Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: an apostle, a royal court and a London park all carry this saint's name.

clue.text: Look at both ends of driveway or be run down

parts.note: to look at is to see

indicators.note: the letters at both ends of the word are its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a driveway or else gets knocked down by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at both ends of' takes D and Y from driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something seedy is shabby and dilapidated.

clue.text: Wherein tackler's tackle

parts.note: a rugby tackler's tackle, slang for genitals, is held in a protective athletic support

explanation.walkthrough: The second 'tackle' is slang for a man's private parts, so the clue asks what holds a sportsman's equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an athletic supporter is the garment that holds and protects a sportsman's genitals.

clue.text: Grass puts Gaff in prison

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a maze traps whoever enters, like a prison
Gaff is the setter, who would call themself I

explanation.surface: An informer gets the setter locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like British slang for an informer but is the cereal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: corn is a member of the grass family of plants.

clue.text: Raise one arm when 19 trip

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters means reading them upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral I
the RAF is an arm of the armed forces
as means when

explanation.surface: Raise an arm in the park to hail someone on an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns IRAFAS upwards; the '19' is a theme nod, a safari park.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a safari is an expedition or trip, usually to see wildlife.

clue.text: Queen keeps fish down

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: The monarch is holding on to some fish and swallowing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like a verb (to swallow) but is the soft feathers that fill an eiderdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the eider duck is the classic source of fine soft feathers used to stuff quilts.

clue.text: He maintains US planes were chic, awfully loud

indicators.note: done awfully, the letters of the phrase are badly jumbled into a new order

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A grumble that some aircraft looked smart but made a terrible din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges WERE CHIC into CREWCHIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage the ground mechanic in charge of an aircraft is given this title.

clue.text: Maybe foil usage in second part of clue

parts.note: a cryptic clue is made of a definition and the mechanism that builds the answer, the latter often being the second part

explanation.surface: A self-referential note about how a cryptic clue is put together.
explanation.walkthrough: A foil is a fencing sword, so using one is fencing; the cryptic half of a clue is its mechanism, usually named by the word for verbal games.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: using a foil, a fencing weapon, is one kind of fencing with blades.

clue.text: Mint stick

definitions.meaning: a common garden herb variety goes by this name plus mint
to stick means to pierce with a pointed weapon

explanation.definitionFit: The herb spearmint takes its name from its pointed leaves, and to stick someone is to stab them.

clue.text: Hope a knockout's content with climax

indicators.note: the content of these words is what they hold inside, so the letters run within them

explanation.surface: A boxer wishes a knockout would settle matters at the fight's high point.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the climax of something is its highest or most intense point.

clue.text: Not the point on which decision may rest

definitions.text: Not the point on which decision may rest

parts.words: Not the point on which decision may rest
parts.note: a close decision is balanced on the sharp side of a blade, not its tip

explanation.walkthrough: A blade has a point and a sharp side; a precarious outcome is said to rest on the latter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a precariously balanced situation is said to be poised on a blade's sharp side.

clue.text: Harry mother by forbidding division

parts.note: Prince Harry's mother was Diana, Princess of Wales, popularly Di
strict, severe and stern in manner

explanation.surface: A prince's mother is seen alongside a stern and disapproving division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' is not to harass but Prince Harry, whose mother was Princess Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a district is an administrative area, a division of a region.

clue.text: US Latinos corrupted by woman from Missouri

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoiled and jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: Some American Latinos are led astray by a woman from Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges US LATINOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonym: a resident of St Louis, the large city in Missouri.

clue.text: Sister declared fate easy to bear

indicators.note: declared means said out loud, so the letters are what is heard

parts.note: a light karma: karma is fate, and light means easy to carry

explanation.surface: A nun says her destiny is not a heavy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a nun of the order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel is such a sister.

clue.text: Subject to trust of land owners

definitions.meaning: a subject of a state is a citizen of it
the ... Trust is the British charity that owns and conserves country houses and land

explanation.definitionFit: A citizen is a national of a country, and the National Trust is Britain's great landowning heritage charity.

clue.text: Estate car storage space for gear

definitions.meaning: the grounds around a country house
a place to leave a vehicle
the setting marked P on an automatic gearbox

explanation.definitionFit: Grounds of a stately home, a parking place, and the P position of an automatic gear selector.

clue.text: A bitter-sweet introduction to the top classes

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the top means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: tart means sharp or bitter in taste

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening letter

explanation.surface: A bittersweet lead-in to the upper classes of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the top' turns ATARTS upwards; 'introduction' takes S from sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: strata are layers or levels, as social classes are.

clue.text: Hank follows southern accent

indicators.note: one piece follows another, coming after it

parts.note: S is southern
a hank or lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A man called Hank picks up a southern accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hank' looks like a name but is a coil of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stress is emphasis or accent on a syllable.

clue.text: Subject to setter following article 19

indicators.note: one piece following another comes after it in the answer

parts.note: the definite article
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's subject, placed after an article about the park.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing 19 is a theme nod: a theme park is another kind of park.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the subject of a talk or essay is its main topic.

clue.text: Stand for freedom, middle England!

parts.note: ease means freedom from difficulty

indicators.note: the middle letter of a seven-letter word is its fourth

explanation.surface: A rally cry to stand up for freedom in the heart of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' takes L from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an artist's stand holds a canvas while painting.

clue.text: Enema must ruin enjoyment for 19

indicators.note: to ruin the words is to wreck them, leaving their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A crude claim that a medical procedure spoils one's fun at the park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' rearranges ENEMA MUST; the trailing 'for 19' nods to the theme, an amusement park.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: amusement is the pleasure or entertainment one takes in something.

clue.text: Take trouble with exercise

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Someone goes to some trouble over their exercise routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to adopt an idea or method is to take it up.

clue.text: Women do well at heart to invest

indicators.note: at heart means inside, so the letters run within these words

explanation.surface: Women basically do well when they put money in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to endow a college is to invest it with funds.

clue.text: Persevering with bottom notes from French interior

parts.note: ass is slang for the backside

indicators.note: an interior piece sits within the other one

parts.note: IOUs are written notes promising repayment
du is French for from the or of the

explanation.surface: Someone keeps at it, writing bottom notes of a French interior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' are IOUs, written promises to pay, not musical notes; 'from French' is the French word du.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone assiduous works diligently and keeps at a task.

clue.text: Motor car storage space for gear

definitions.meaning: to motor is to travel by car
the strip of private ground outside a house where a car is left
the setting marked D on an automatic gearbox

explanation.definitionFit: Travel by car, the private approach where a car stands, and the D position of an automatic selector.

clue.text: It's a condition that I get mental stimulation

indicators.note: stimulated letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient claims their medical condition comes from too much brain activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stimulation' rearranges I and MENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an illness or disorder is a medical condition.

clue.text: Seven points for novelty

parts.note: the first three of seven compass points: north, east, west
the other four compass points: north, east, south, south

explanation.surface: A judge awards a score of seven for originality.
explanation.walkthrough: The points are compass points, each giving its initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: novelty is the quality of being new and unfamiliar.
